title: The Riemann hypothesis
summary: Does every nontrivial zero of the zeta function have real part one half.
statement: For the analytically continued Riemann zeta function ζ(s), prove or disprove that every nontrivial zero has real part 1/2.

title: P versus NP
summary: Can every problem whose answer is checked quickly also be solved quickly.
statement: Does every decision problem whose proposed solutions can be verified in polynomial time by a deterministic Turing machine also admit a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm; equivalently, is P = NP?

title: Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness
summary: Does smooth three-dimensional fluid data stay smooth for all time.
statement: For smooth, divergence-free initial velocity with finite energy in three dimensions, do the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations always have a global smooth solution, or can a finite-time singularity form?

title: The Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture
summary: Do the rational points on an elliptic curve match the vanishing of its L-function at one.
statement: For every elliptic curve E over the rational numbers, is the rank of E(Q) equal to the order of vanishing of its Hasse–Weil L-function L(E,s) at s = 1?

title: The Hodge conjecture
summary: Which cohomology classes on a projective algebraic variety come from algebraic cycles.
statement: For every smooth projective complex variety, is each rational cohomology class of type (p,p) a rational linear combination of classes of algebraic cycles?

title: Yang-Mills existence and mass gap
summary: Does a mathematically complete quantum Yang-Mills theory exist with a positive mass gap.
statement: For every compact simple gauge group, construct a nontrivial quantum Yang–Mills theory on four-dimensional spacetime satisfying the accepted axioms and prove that its spectrum has a positive mass gap.

title: The Poincaré conjecture
summary: Is every simply connected closed three-manifold homeomorphic to the three-sphere.

title: The Collatz conjecture
summary: Does every positive integer reach one under halving and 3n plus 1.
statement: Starting from any positive integer n, repeatedly replace an even value by n/2 and an odd value by 3n+1. Must the sequence reach 1?

title: The Goldbach conjecture
summary: Is every even integer greater than two a sum of two primes.
statement: Is every even integer greater than 2 expressible as the sum of two prime numbers?

title: The twin prime conjecture
summary: Are there infinitely many prime pairs that differ by two.
statement: Are there infinitely many primes p for which p+2 is also prime?

title: The abc conjecture
summary: For coprime a, b, and c with a plus b equals c, how tightly does the radical of abc bound c.

title: The perfect cuboid
summary: Can a rectangular box have integer edges, face diagonals, and space diagonal.
statement: Do positive integers a, b, and c exist such that a, b, c, √(a²+b²), √(a²+c²), √(b²+c²), and √(a²+b²+c²) are all integers?

title: The Hadwiger conjecture
summary: Does every graph of chromatic number k contain a complete minor of order k.
statement: For every finite graph G of chromatic number k, does G contain the complete graph K_k as a minor?

title: The Erdős-Straus conjecture
summary: Is 4 divided by n always a sum of three positive unit fractions for n greater than one.
statement: For every integer n greater than 1, do positive integers x, y, z exist with 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z?

title: Regularity of the 3x plus 1 map
summary: Is there a structure theorem behind the map that keeps returning to one.
statement: For the map T(n)=n/2 when n is even and T(n)=(3n+1)/2 when n is odd, can the orbit structure of every positive integer be proved to enter the cycle 1→2→1?

title: Infinitely many perfect numbers
summary: Are there infinitely many numbers equal to the sum of their proper divisors.
statement: Are there infinitely many even perfect numbers; equivalently, are there infinitely many primes p for which 2^p−1 is prime?

title: The existence of Einstein metrics
summary: Which smooth manifolds carry a metric whose Ricci curvature is a constant multiple of the metric.
statement: Which smooth compact manifolds admit a Riemannian metric whose Ricci tensor is a constant multiple of the metric, and what geometric obstructions characterize existence?

title: The chromatic number of the plane
summary: How many colors are needed so that points one unit apart never share a color.
statement: What is the chromatic number of the Euclidean plane when every pair of points at distance exactly one must receive different colors?

label: C1
title: The crooked needle
summary: Which unit-length rectifiable curve maximizes the chance of crossing at least one randomly placed ruled line?
statement: Let γ be any rectifiable plane curve of total length 1. Rotate γ uniformly through [0, π) and translate it by a uniformly random offset modulo 1 across parallel lines spaced 1 apart. The expected crossing count is 2/π, but the probability of at least one transverse crossing depends on γ. Which curve maximizes that probability, and what proof establishes optimality?
approach: Count crossings first: the integral-geometric mean is 2/π, so the gap between the mean count and the chance of any crossing is the room to optimize.

label: C2
title: The silent board
summary: Which Galton-board peg-removal patterns give exactly equal probability to every final bin?
statement: Which Galton-board peg-removal patterns give exactly equal probability to every final bin?
approach: Track each row as an exact rational distribution; a Julia search over every removal mask gives a small-n witness, while a proof must explain all n.

label: C3
title: The pile's memory
summary: What fraction of the identity sandpile on a 2n × 2n grid has height exactly two as n grows?
statement: What fraction of the identity sandpile on a 2n × 2n grid has height exactly two as n grows?
approach: Use the burning test and the identity's recurrent structure, then compare exact finite grids with a provable finite-size bound.

label: C4
title: The butterfly's period
summary: At what first ρ does the Lorenz return map acquire a primitive orbit of period three?
statement: At what first ρ does the Lorenz return map acquire a primitive orbit of period three?
approach: Locate a primitive fixed point of Pρ³, then enclose all three section points and the intervening flow with interval arithmetic.

label: C5
title: The duelist's dice
problemType: Proof or exhaustive search with proof of exhaustiveness
summary: Can three fair six-sided dice form a non-transitive cycle with each win probability exactly two thirds?
statement: Can three fair six-sided dice form a non-transitive cycle with each win probability exactly two thirds?
approach: Write each pairwise win count as an integer out of 36, use the required two-thirds count to constrain the face orderings, and make an exhaustive search independently checkable.

title: The Hubble tension
summary: Is the early–late disagreement in H₀ new physics, a systematic error, or a statistical fluctuation?
statement: Determine whether the disagreement between the local distance-ladder value of H₀ and the value inferred from the cosmic microwave background under ΛCDM is caused by new physics, unrecognized systematics, or statistical fluctuation. Give a quantitative account that identifies which observations or calibrations distinguish the possibilities.

title: Five billion years of solar-system stability
summary: Can the probability of planetary instability over five billion years be bounded beyond current numerical ensembles?
statement: For an ensemble of initial conditions consistent with present orbital measurements, determine a controlled probability or rigorous interval for a terrestrial-planet collision, ejection, or clearly specified instability within the next five billion years. Include the Moon and general-relativistic corrections, and quantify how observational covariance and model choices change the result.

sources.title: Laskar and Gastineau, five-gigayear integrations, Nature 2009
Laskar and Gastineau, study summary and reported ensemble

title: The dark-halo cusp–core problem
summary: Can a single, observationally consistent model explain the diversity of inner dark-matter density profiles?
statement: Determine whether collisionless ΛCDM together with baryonic feedback can reproduce the observed range of inner density profiles in dwarf and low-surface-brightness galaxies, including their rotation curves, without conflicting with independent constraints. If it cannot, identify which additional dark-matter or gravitational ingredient is required and quantify the evidence against observational systematics.

sources.title: Bullock and Boylan-Kolchin, Small-Scale Challenges to ΛCDM, 2017

title: The lazy scrambler's horizon
summary: How many lazy random turns bring a solved cube within total-variation distance 1/4 of uniform?
label: C6
statement: Start at the solved fixed-center 3×3×3 cube. At each step, stay put with probability 1/2; otherwise choose uniformly one of the 18 face turns U, U², U′, …, B′. Determine the least n for which the distribution of cube positions is within total-variation distance 1/4 of uniform, or prove the tightest possible lower and upper bounds. The arena's retirement-with-honors rule applies if this exact lazy walk was resolved earlier.
approach: Use cube symmetries, spectral bounds, coupling, or certified computation. Distinguish this lazy chain from the independent-turn walk in the cited lower-bound paper; if an earlier result already settles the exact chain, record its source and retire C6 with honors.

sources.title: Qu, Rokicki, and Yang, Rubik's Cube Scrambling Requires at Least 26 Random Moves
Cube group, generators, and God's-number history

title: Uniqueness of the figure-eight choreography
summary: Is the equal-mass figure eight the unique global minimizer in its symmetry class, up to the natural symmetries?
label: C7
statement: In the planar Newtonian three-body problem with equal masses and center of mass fixed at zero, normalize the total mass and period and impose the reflection and choreography symmetries used to construct the figure-eight orbit. Determine whether the Chenciner–Montgomery orbit is the unique global minimizer of the Newtonian action in this class, modulo rotation, time shift, and relabeling. Prove uniqueness or exhibit a distinct minimizer.
approach: The existence proof and a computer-assisted local-uniqueness theorem do not classify every global minimizer. Establish global bounds in the stated symmetry class or construct a second admissible orbit with a verified action comparison.

sources.title: Kapela and Zgliczyński, computer-assisted local uniqueness
Simó, choreographies of the planar three-body problem
